name: email-constraint-mailbox-with-leading-dot-host-invalid
description: permittedSubtrees rfc822Name is 'foo@.example.com' — a mailbox-form constraint (carrying a local-part 'foo') whose host part has a leading dot. The leading-dot form ('.example.com') is only defined for host-only constraints (RFC 5280 §4.2.1.10 example: '.example.com' indicates all Internet mail addresses in the domain). Combining a specific local-part with a leading-dot host is not a defined constraint shape. The leaf's SAN 'foo@bar.example.com' is a well-formed mailbox at bar.example.com; the constraint either parses as malformed (UNSUPPORTED_NAME_SYNTAX) or, if treated literally, fails to match (the leaf's host is 'bar.example.com', not '.example.com'). Either way the leaf must be rejected.
notes: Probes how each validator parses the 'local-part@.host' constraint form. Strict parsers reject it as syntactically ill-formed; lax parsers may strip the leading dot and treat it as 'foo@example.com', then reject the leaf for host mismatch. Either response gives the right outcome here; a parser that interprets the leading dot as 'any subdomain' would erroneously accept 'foo@bar.example.com'.
